issues.description: Returning bare nil *result on leader-panic violates run()'s postcondition and pushes nil-deref risk to callers
issues.detail: When CompareAndSwap fails and t.result.Load() is nil, the new code returns nil. Every other run() exit yields a non-nil *result and downstream callers rely on that. The fix should return a sentinel result with Fatal set, not nil — otherwise the nil-deref simply moves one layer up.

issues.description: The t.result lifecycle invariant is unstated; the race between Load and use is patched, not reasoned
issues.detail: The fix depends on the leader CASing t.result back to nil on panic, but that invariant is not documented at the call site or module boundary. The two branches (pending-output and CAS-failure) now handle the same race inconsistently. State the t.result state machine and memory ordering, or unify the snapshot path.

issues.description: Cycle detection is skipped on the CAS-failure slow path where it previously ran
issues.detail: Before the refactor, checkCycle ran whenever t.result.Load() was non-nil at entry. After the change, when CAS fails and a waiter joins an already-pending task, control jumps straight to waitUntilDone with no checkCycle. A caller in a cycle will now deadlock on output.done instead of returning ErrCycle.

issues.description: No regression test exercises the panicking-leader-with-waiters race
issues.detail: A concurrency bug that produced a nil deref is being fixed with zero new tests. Add a deterministic reproducer: inject a panic in the leader, have N waiters contend, and assert each gets a sensible error rather than nil or panic. Without this, the fix will regress silently.

issues.description: Comment 'Leader panicked but we did see a result' inverts the meaning of its branch
issues.detail: The surrounding logic fires precisely when no result was observed. The comment should read 'did not see a result'. Comments are part of the spec; an inverted comment on a subtle concurrency branch will mislead maintainers about when this path fires and whether returning nil is intended.

issues.description: Inner `output := t.result.Load()` shadows the outer named return and obscures roles
issues.detail: Inside the CAS-failure branch a new `output` shadows the function's named return. The two variables represent different roles (this goroutine's own result vs. the leader's). Rename the inner one (e.g., `leader`) to make the relationship explicit and prevent accidental misuse.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this PR is NEEDS-WORK. The checkCycle extraction is a fine cleanup, but the race fix is half-done: returning bare nil from run() on leader-panic relocates the nil-deref into every caller rather than eliminating it, and the underlying t.result lifecycle invariant is never stated. Liskov additionally observes that cycle detection is now skipped on the CAS-failure path, introducing a deadlock regression. Required changes: return a Fatal-carrying sentinel instead of nil, reinstate checkCycle on the slow path, document the t.result state machine, fix the inverted comment, and add a deterministic regression test for the panicking-leader case.
